clue.text: Save seafood cold rather than hot

indicators.note: C for cold is put where H for hot stood, as on a tap

parts.note: shrimp is a kind of seafood

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a shrimp cocktail chilled instead of cooking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold rather than hot' swaps the H of SHRIMP for C, the tap letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise, to put money by.

clue.text: Bird in old attic, not dead, fluttering about

indicators.note: fluttering about suggests the letters are tossed into a new arrangement
not says the dead abbreviation is removed from the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird trapped in an old attic, alive and flapping around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not dead' removes D from OLD ATTIC, then 'fluttering about' rearranges OLATTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small European bird of the tit family.

clue.text: Very dark, curly, topless

indicators.note: topless says the first letter, the top of a down entry, is removed

parts.note: kinky hair is tightly curled

explanation.surface: A risqué description of a dark-haired topless figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes K from KINKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink is black, so inky means intensely dark.

clue.text: Stop Mrs Grundy outside English class

indicators.note: outside says the prude's letters surround the others

parts.note: Mrs Grundy is the proverbial narrow-minded prude from an old English play
CL is the abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: Mrs Grundy halts an English lesson from outside the room.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Grundy, from Thomas Morton's play Speed the Plough, stands for a priggish moraliser; 'outside' wraps PRUDE round E and CL.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude is to prevent or rule out in advance.

clue.text: Attack doctor in Australian hospital

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the Australian abbreviation

parts.note: Aus is the short form of Australian
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A medic assaulted inside a hospital Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attack' reads as a verb on the doctor, but it is the definition; MB is the medical degree standing for any doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a surprise attack from hiding.

clue.text: Be responsible for key

explanation.surface: Taking charge of a key.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer for something is to be accountable for it; a key is the list of solutions to a test.

clue.text: See here

parts.note: a see is a diocese, so 'here' points to the area a bishop governs

explanation.walkthrough: 'See here' reads as 'look at this', but a see is a church district.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, the district under one bishop.

clue.text: Unjustified slander spoken roughly

indicators.note: unjustified, like text not lined up, signals the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An unfair slander growled in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unjustified' rearranges SLANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To snarl is to speak in a rough, angry growl.

clue.text: Candour shown by old German head

parts.note: the Franks were an ancient Germanic people
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: An outspoken old German headmaster praised for honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' means a headland, as in Dungeness or Orford Ness on the English coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankness and candour are synonyms for open honesty.

clue.text: Garnish-fresh one's been prepared

indicators.note: prepared says the letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written
one is I and 's stands for is or has, giving I and S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook announcing the fresh garnish is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' gives IS (I + 's); 'prepared' rearranges FRESH, IS, BEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fines herbes are a French mix of chopped herbs used to garnish dishes.

clue.text: Contraction is used in charts, on reflection

indicators.note: reflection reverses an image, so the letters are read backwards
used in means the S is placed inside the word for charts

parts.note: maps are charts
is shortens to 's, as in it's

explanation.surface: Someone thinks again about how 'is' is used in charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' puts S inside MAPS, giving MSAPS; 'on reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is a sudden involuntary muscle contraction.

clue.text: Bachelor put off by gross barnstorming Venus

indicators.note: gross, meaning crude or distorted, signals the letters are rearranged
put off says the bachelor's letter is removed

explanation.surface: A bachelor repelled by a crude, showy Venus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' removes B from BARNSTORMING; 'gross' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the bright planet seen at dawn, called the morning star.

clue.text: Letter brought over from uncle to niece

indicators.note: brought over says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A letter passed from an uncle to his niece.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ETON spans 'uncLE TO Niece'; 'brought over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a short written message, a letter.

clue.text: Manual: first half of book involved with cellular changes

indicators.note: changes says the gathered letters are rearranged
the first half of the four-letter word book is its first two letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A biology manual whose opening half deals with changes in cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first half of' takes BO from 'book'; 'changes' rearranges BO plus CELLULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-collar work is manual labour, as opposed to office work.

clue.text: Allocate short time in holiday area

indicators.note: in places the short time inside the holiday area

parts.note: the seaside is a typical place for a holiday
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Booking a brief break by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short time' is the usual crossword shorthand for the single letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside is to reserve or earmark something for a purpose.

clue.text: Shoot up in Scottish island hosting rock concert finally

indicators.note: hosting says the island holds the rock inside it

parts.note: Skye is an island in the Scottish Hebrides
taken as written

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Hebridean island stages a rock concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is one of the Inner Hebrides; 'rock' looks like part of the concert but goes in as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To skyrocket is to rise very fast, like a firework.

clue.text: Bones a detective found in New England state

indicators.note: found in says the article and detective sit inside the state

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, a New England state
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective discovers skeletal remains in New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' looks like a nickname for a doctor, but it is the plural of radius.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone; the plural names two such bones.

clue.text: Novel way to hold up manoeuvres by Franco

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece that holds up another sits beneath it
manoeuvres suggests the letters are moved around

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Franco's troop manoeuvres held up on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges FRANCO into CRANFO; 'to hold up' puts RD below it. Cranford is Elizabeth Gaskell's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranford is an 1853 work of fiction by Elizabeth Gaskell.

clue.text: Outdated article about side

annotationWithheld.why: 'Outdated article about side' (5): YE (outdated article) around MEN (side) gives YMENE, which must also be reversed for ENEMY; 'about' would be both the container and the reversal indicator, a word doing two jobs.

clue.text: Squeeze's message initially deleted — obscene

indicators.note: initially deleted removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: a text is a phone message
rude means crude or obscene

explanation.surface: A squeeze sends a crude message and then deletes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeeze' looks like a lover; 'initially deleted' removes T from TEXT.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to squeeze or force out through an opening.

clue.text: Unexpectedly get Capri ticket

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters land in a surprising new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unexpected chance to win a ticket to Capri.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' rearranges GET CAPRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A price tag is the label, or ticket, showing what something costs.

clue.text: Plane possibly carrying two King's — one a Kirk devotee?

indicators.note: carrying says the tree holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a plane is one example of a tree

indicators.note: two means the king's letter appears twice

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An aeroplane carrying two kings and a Kirk fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts KKI inside TREE; Captain Kirk commands the Enterprise in Star Trek.
explanation.definitionFit: A Star Trek fan devoted to its Captain Kirk is called by this nickname.

clue.text: Limits to Surrey supporting county magazine

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece is written beneath

parts.note: Glos is the abbreviation of Gloucestershire, an English county

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Surrey's borders propping up a neighbouring county's magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits to' gives SY, the first and last letters of 'Surrey'; 'supporting' puts it under GLOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy is a magazine printed on shiny paper.

clue.text: Account, finally, for VPL?

explanation.surface: A note on underwear lines at the foot of a statement.
explanation.walkthrough: VPL is 'visible panty line', a line seen on the seat; the question mark flags the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The final figure on an account is its net result; a VPL is literally a line on a person's rear.

clue.text: Lie evident in sincere statement

indicators.note: evident in says the letters can be seen sitting inside the words

explanation.surface: A lie exposed in what claimed to be an honest statement.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'sinceRE STatement'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rest is to lie down and relax.

clue.text: Book by American, very big

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very big

explanation.surface: A huge book by an American author.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Fast food required by son

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
tuck is British slang for food, especially schoolchildren's snacks

explanation.surface: A boy demands fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: TUCK is British school slang for snacks; 'fast' means fixed firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held fast is firmly fixed and unable to move.

clue.text: Oxford sewer working at last

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of shoe, a sewer is one who stitches, and a last is the foot-shaped form a cobbler works on

explanation.surface: Oxford's drains are finally functioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain but means a stitcher; the last is a cobbler's wooden foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler stitches Oxford brogues over a last.

clue.text: Quality shown by good number of competitors?

definitions.note: here the noun meaning the upper classes, an old collective sense

parts.note: the entry for a race is the number of competitors in it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a big field shows the quality of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quality' is the old phrase 'the quality', meaning people of rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the well-born upper class, once called 'the quality'.

clue.text: Cloth, bit from dark overcoat, not large

indicators.note: a bit from the word means just its first letter
not says the large abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: an ulster is a long loose overcoat
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A scrap torn from a dark coat, not a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit from' takes D; 'not large' removes L from ULSTER, leaving USTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A duster is a cloth used for wiping dust off surfaces.
